facts.raw_span: A woman in her 70s presented with a pruritic and painful periorbital eruption that had lasted 1 month
scaly, crusted pink plaques that involved the periorbital skin
Punch biopsy from the left upper eyelid demonstrated vacuolar interface dermatitis with follicular involvement and epidermal atrophy
lenalidomide (severely worsened platelet count, with a nadir of 28 ×10^3/μL)

scaly, crusted pink plaques that involved the periorbital skin
Punch biopsy from the left upper eyelid demonstrated vacuolar interface dermatitis with follicular involvement and epidermal atrophy
lenalidomide (severely worsened platelet count, with a nadir of 28 ×10^3/μL)

concepts.why: The patient's presentation of a pruritic and painful periorbital eruption with scaly, crusted pink plaques and vacuolar interface dermatitis on biopsy is consistent with discoid lupus erythematosus, a common manifestation of lupus nephritis.
The patient's periorbital eruption with scaly, crusted pink plaques could be a manifestation of cutaneous T-cell lymphoma, particularly given the history of acute myeloid leukemia.

The patient's history of acute myeloid leukemia and chemotherapy-induced peripheral neuropathy raises the possibility of graft-versus-host disease, which could manifest with skin symptoms similar to those described.
The patient's history of lupus nephritis and exposure to hydroxychloroquine, which can induce lupus-like symptoms, suggests the possibility of drug-induced lupus erythematosus.
The patient's history of lenalidomide treatment and development of a skin rash suggests the possibility of a lenalidomide-induced skin rash.
The patient's history of deep vein thrombosis could be related to the skin changes observed, particularly if the DVT has caused chronic venous insufficiency.
The patient's history of diverticulitis could be related to the skin manifestations observed, although this is less common.
The patient's history of postcolectomy diarrhea could be related to the skin changes observed, particularly if the diarrhea has caused skin irritation or malabsorption.
It explains the uncovered finding of lupus nephritis and diverticulitis, which are associated with Sjögren's syndrome.
